instruction: We represent Trenex Flight Provisions, LLC, the buyer and maker of the Seller Note, in its stock purchase from Dulaix Hospitality Holdings, Inc. Please review all seven documents in the folder and prepare a memo to me identifying each issue you find. For each, note where it appears (document and section), explain why it matters for Trenex, and recommend a fix. We need this to protect the client's position before the deal closes.

rubric.text: The response concludes that Trenex's October 9, 2026 dispute letter was delivered outside the 30-day period after the Closing Statement was delivered on September 2, 2026, so Seller can treat the Closing Statement as final and binding and defeat the $1,150,000 working capital dispute. It identifies where this arises (SPA Section 2.5(b) or the October 2026 dispute letter), explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that closing the Parent Merger will be a Change of Control Event of Default under the Seller Note, allowing Dulaix to accelerate the note, and that the SPA acknowledgement of the Parent Merger does not waive this Note default. It identifies where this arises (SPA Section 6.12 or Seller Note Section 1 / 5.1(g)), explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the Key Employee Agreement non-solicit, by using the SPA definition of Key Customers, protects only the ten largest fiscal 2025 airline customers and leaves Okafor-Brandt free to solicit the Company's other customers, which is narrower than the all-customer scope in the letter of intent. It identifies where this arises (Key Employee Agreement Section 5.2 or SPA Section 1.1), explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that Trenex's indemnity for the Seller Credit Support Obligations is excluded from the $4,800,000 Buyer cap and extends to obligations arising before the Closing, so Trenex has uncapped liability for Dulaix's guarantee exposure, including pre-closing defaults. It identifies where this arises (SPA Section 1.1, 9.3(c) or 9.5(b)), explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that because tax representation survival is tied to the Seller Note Maturity Date, twelve months after issue, Trenex's tax indemnity claims expire around August 3, 2027. This is shorter than the 18-month general survival period and before many pre-closing tax assessments could arise. It identifies where this arises (SPA Section 9.1(b) or Seller Note Section 2.1), explains why this matters to the client, and recommends a fix.
hints: Maturity Date of the Seller Note

rubric.text: The response states that the purchase price is $48,000,000, consisting of $42,000,000 in cash and a $6,000,000 Seller Note.
The response is a memo addressed to the supervising partner that presents each issue as a separately identified item.
The response claims that Trenex's October 9, 2026 dispute letter was delivered within the SPA's Closing Statement dispute period.
The response claims that SPA Section 6.12 waives, or provides Holder consent to, a Change of Control default under the Seller Note arising from the Parent Merger.
